The rules above still apply. For this one response, write the first message about the file just opened or imported, by the person or by a tool call of mine. Report and offer from the report and the picture, and change nothing the person has not asked for.

The report separates four sources. The app-computed opening outcome (loadFacts, loads, and objects) establishes what arrived and how the selected printer, material and print settings changed. A load's withSettings only says the app requested settings, not that it applied them; claim they were applied only when loadFacts.settingsOutcome says applied. If that outcome is absent, leave the application of settings uncertain. The current workspace establishes what is selected now; setupPrinters lists printer models the person has set up in JusPrin. Neither a selection nor that list proves which physical machine they intend to use. The raw messages.items contain Orca's dialog title and text, offered buttons, and the answer JusPrin supplied automatically. The person did not choose that answer and may never have seen the dialog. The file's details.description and details.profileDescription are author notes: claims from the file, not proof that their advice was applied. The picture, when present, is the active plate after the load, rendered from the iso view.

Look at the attached picture when there is one. From it and the report, make an educated guess at what the object is, what it is likely for, and how it should be sliced (orientation, supports, strength), and say it as a guess. Check the selected printer, filament and process presets and the plate type against that guess, against the printers the person has set up, and against the presets available (presets_list); when one looks wrong for this print, say which and suggest the one to use, without changing it.

Explain where a warning came from when the report shows it: what the file contains, what I noticed while loading it, whether its settings were applied, and what still needs checking. | --- | --- |

| Settings were substituted with supported values | Usually omit when completed successfully. Explain briefly if the result materially changes the print or still needs a choice. |
| “Customized Preset” or a file setting has no installed match | This alone does not establish that machine commands changed. Use the final selected printer and material to judge the consequence. |

---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at

content.text:
## 1. Chat panel width: done

The chat panel used to open at 320 px, which is also the narrowest you can drag it to. It now opens at 429 px, the width of the chat dock's Figma frame; the AgentUI preview tests already render the chat at that width. I added it as a new design token, `component.agentPane.width`, next to `minWidth`, the same way the left pane has both. Dragging still stops at 320, and a window too small for 429 still shrinks the panel down to 320.

- Commit `74c1335d8f` on jusprin-newui. It's local only, not pushed.
- Both token tests pass (`shell_theme_tests` and `brand_tokens_tests`).
- I launched a renamed copy of the new build with a scratch data folder and opened a cube. In a 1,403-point-wide window the chat panel was about 430 points wide. Your own running JusPrin was not touched.

## 2. The opening message after an import

I found the exact data the agent got for your screenshot in the saved conversation. Here is what it was told:

- You used **Import Object** to add arrow_headband.3mf to the "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2" setup. Its settings outcome was "geometry only", which is normal for Import Object.
- It got three notices from OrcaSlicer: the "laid over the boundary of plate" error, which arrived twice, and an object-info notice ("Size: 253.913 x 251.999 x 10 mm … <Error></Error>").
- It got the list of printers you have set up: two Kobra 3s, an A1, the A1 mini, a K1 and a Qidi X-Plus 4. It got **names only, no bed sizes**.

What makes the reply awkward, and where each problem comes from:

1. **It ends with a vague menu: "a larger printer, or split / resized".** This is the biggest problem. The bundled profiles say your A1 bed is 256 × 256 mm, the Kobra 3 is 255 × 255 and the X-Plus 4 is 305 × 305. All three fit a 254 × 252 headband. The agent couldn't say "it fits your A1" because it was never told any bed size. The file-loaded skill (its instructions for the first message after a file loads) does ask it to suggest the printer to use, but the facts it would need are missing.
2. **It narrates plumbing.** It wrote "I loaded it as geometry only, so the file's print settings were not applied", but you chose Import, so that is expected. The skill invites this with "Explain where a warning came from: … whether its settings were applied", even though a row in the skill's own table says to explain this only when it changes the next step. The two lines contradict each other.
3. **It speculates and hedges.** The skill requires a guess at what the object is, what it's for, and how to orient and support it. This part is already lying flat and 10 mm tall, and its size problem blocks everything else. So the guess turned into filler like "probably", "gently arched" and "unless you later turn it upright".
4. **It says the fit problem twice**, in the first paragraph and again in the second.
5. **"Orca reported…"** breaks the core prompt's own first-person rule.
6. **It bolds 15 phrases.** The prompt says "bold is fine" and sets no limit.

What the reply should have looked like:

> This headband is 254 × 252 mm, too big for the A1 mini's 180 × 180 mm bed. It fits your Bambu Lab A1 (256 × 256 mm). Want me to switch the project to the A1?

### Fixes I'd propose, most important first

- **A. Give the agent the fit facts.** The app would work out, for the selected printer and each printer you've set up, the bed size and whether each object fits. That goes into the file report. It follows your rule that situational text comes from the app's data, not the standing prompt. Without it, no prompt wording can produce the reply above. This is fork code, so nothing is touched in OrcaSlicer-owned files.
- **B. Cut the file-loaded skill down.** Make the object/purpose guess conditional, only when nothing blocks and it changes the setup. Remove the "explain where a warning came from" sentence. Keep one rule: name the most important problem once, then give one concrete next step.
- **C. Clean up the report.** Remove the duplicate notice. Leave out the object-info notice, since its numbers are already in `objects`.
- **D. Optionally, limit bold in the core prompt** (for example, "bold at most one phrase"). This would change every reply, not just this one, so it's a bigger decision.

Testing: I can run A–C against the recorded request with no model calls. Checking the actual wording needs live model runs, which need your OK for a specific batch. I'd suggest this file plus two or three other file-load cases, a few runs each, before and after.

Three things I need from you:
1. Should I do A, B and C together, or A first by itself?
2. Should the opening message ever guess what the object is for when nothing is blocking? Or should it just ask when the purpose matters?
3. Do you want D, or should bold stay as it is?

# File-loaded opening message: offline experiment

Written 2026-10-19 on `jusprin-newui` at 74c1335d8f. Untracked working doc.

## What was tested

The case is Kenneth's import of `arrow_headband.3mf` onto "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2". The object is 253.9 × 252.0 × 10 mm and the bed is 180 × 180 mm. The app's first message, from gpt-5.4-mini (the default in `OpenAIResponsesAgent.hpp`), was awkward: it narrated how the file was loaded, guessed at the object and its slicing, stated the fit problem twice, ended with a menu of options and bolded 11 phrases.

I rebuilt the request from the code and from the saved conversation (`~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/projects/p-3a6318012e2f827f-2d66758b462735b3/current-state.json`):

- the system prompt from `projectInstructions.ts`;
- the 28 tools from `tests/project_prompt/project_tools.json`;
- the file report exactly as saved;
- a `<workspace>` block written by hand from the saved checkpoint;
- the file-loaded skill text plus the "nothing is recorded about what this print is for" sentence.

Each run was a fresh Opus 5.5 subagent that saw only that request, never this critique. Three limits apply:

- The picture is a crop of Kenneth's screenshot, not the app's own render.
- Tool calls could not be answered, so a run that wanted a call named it and replied from what it had.
- Opus 5.5 is a far stronger model than gpt-5.4-mini. Only a live batch on gpt-5.4-mini shows whether these changes carry over to it.

## Variants

- **v0 (control):** the request as the app sent it.
- **v1a (data only):** the same skill, but the report is changed in two ways. Each `setupPrinters` entry gains `bedMm`, the usable bed after the profile's excluded areas. The object gains `fitsSelectedPrinter: false` and `fitsOn: ["Bambu Lab A1", "Qidi X-Plus 4"]`. The duplicate boundary notice and the object-info notice (whose numbers are already in `objects`) are removed.
- **v1b (data + skill):** v1a's report plus the rewritten skill (diff at the end).

The Kobra 3 is a trap for raw bed sizes. Its profile says 255 × 255 mm but excludes a 2 mm border, so only 251 mm is usable and the 254 mm headband does not fit. A field holding the nominal bed size would have told the model it fits. The app has to report the result of the fit check, not just the size.

## Results (3 runs each)

| | words | bold phrases | names A1 as the fix | object guess | PLA/PETG tangent | "when I opened the file I warned" | ends with one question |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-5.4-mini, original | 132 | 11 | no ("a larger printer") | yes | no | "Orca reported" | no (a menu) |
| v0 Opus | 190–230 | 3–5 | 3/3 (2 of 3 wrongly call the Kobra 3 too small... which happens to be right, for the wrong reason) | 3/3 | 3/3 | 2/3 | 3/3 |
| v1a Opus | 200–260 | 3–6 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 2/3 |
| v1b Opus | 60–110 | 2–4 | 3/3 | 1/3, one sentence | 0/3 | 0/3 | 3/3 |

Conclusions:

- The data change makes the printer advice correct: bed sizes, the Kobra 3's exclusion, the 1 mm margin on the A1.
- The skill rewrite is what fixes the length and the awkward parts. The current skill tells the model to guess the object and its slicing, and to explain where a warning came from, so even Opus does both.
- Bold was not changed. Opus bolds 2–6 phrases under the same prompt, and the saved gpt replies on this machine bold heavily on Sep 30 and since Oct 12 (both before and after "bold are fine" was added on Oct 15) but not at all from Oct 1 to 10. The saved conversations don't record which model or prompt produced each reply, so the cause can't be pinned without live runs.

## Representative replies

### gpt-5.4-mini, original (what Kenneth saw)

> The big issue is fit: the model is **253.9 × 252.0 × 10 mm**, and Orca reported it **extends past the plate boundary**. I loaded it as **geometry only**, so the file's print settings were **not** applied.
>
> From the picture and the name, I'd guess this is a **headband / arched wearable part**. It probably wants to be printed **flat or gently arched**, with the **largest flat face on the bed** and **no supports** unless you later turn it upright. Right now it also looks much too wide for the **A1 mini** plate setup, so the selected printer/preset combo may be the wrong choice for this model.

### v0, Opus, run 2

> **This won't fit on the printer that's selected now.** The headband is about 254 × 252 mm across. The selected printer, the Bambu Lab A1 mini, has a bed of only 180 × 180 mm. That's why I showed the "laid over the boundary of plate" error when the file opened. Nothing has fixed it yet, and turning the model on the bed won't help, because the arrow already runs corner to corner.
>

> - **Bambu Lab A1** (256 × 256 mm bed): it fits, but with only about a millimetre to spare on each side. There's no room for a brim, the extra ring of plastic some prints use to grip the bed.
> - **Qidi X-Plus 4** (305 × 305 mm bed): it fits with room to spare.

# File-loaded opening message: offline experiments

Untracked working doc, 2026-10-19, `jusprin-newui` at 74c1335d8f. All replies from round 2 are in `file-loaded-opening-replies.md` next to this file. Nothing in the repository has been changed for this.

## The question

When a person opens or imports a file, the app sends the agent a file-load report, a `<workspace>` block, a picture of the plate and the file-loaded skill (the instructions for that one message). The agent then writes its first message. On Kenneth's headband import that message was awkward and missed the obvious fix. Round 1 found one missing fact (bed sizes). Kenneth's objection was that adding one field per problem we happen to hit is patchwork. Round 2 therefore chooses the report's facts from everything the app can know, and tests on several different files instead of one.

## Method

- **Real requests.** I pointed a test copy of the app (its own data folder, Kenneth's printers and presets, A1 mini selected) at a local server that saves each request and answers with an error (`JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT`). Opening a file then records the exact request the app would send to gpt-5.4-mini: system prompt, 28 tools, report, workspace block, the app's own render and the skill. Nothing was sent to OpenAI.
- **Extra facts from the app itself.** For each file I also called the app's own MCP tools (`object_analyze` with mesh, fit and orientations; `workspace_inspect`). I read the printers' beds from their profiles and the 3MF's own settings from inside the file.
- **Stand-in model.** Each request went to a fresh Opus 5.5 subagent that saw only that request and picture. It gets one run per case and variant. Tool calls could not be answered.
- **Variants.**
  - **v0:** the request unchanged.
  - **v1:** the rewritten skill.
  - **v2:** the rewritten skill plus the chosen facts.

Limits: Opus 5.5 is much stronger than gpt-5.4-mini, there is one run per cell, and I judged the replies myself. A live gpt-5.4-mini batch is what would settle it. That needs Kenneth's approval.

## Cases

| Case | File | Situation |
|---|---|---|
| battery | Battery_Holder_AAAandAA.stl | Plain part, nothing wrong |
| octopus | Octopus_v6.stl | Print-in-place figure, nothing wrong |
| tiny | Swanky Wolt-Blad.stl | 22 mm L-piece standing on thin edges |
| yoda | YodaFigure.stl | 150 mm figure, 1.26M triangles, simplify notice |
| frame_parts | All frame parts.3mf | PrusaSlicer 3MF; JusPrin loads geometry only; 32 parts |
| headband | arrow_headband.3mf (imported) | Too big for the A1 mini (Kenneth's case) |
| two_color | little_boxes_two_color.3mf | Opening it switched to the file's "MyKlipper 0.6 nozzle" and PA-CF; the object is partly off the plate |
| bambu_project | FFZW迫击炮P1X1系列无裙边.3mf | Bambu P1S project, 13 parts, collision warning, Chinese text |

## How the facts were chosen

A read-only survey listed everything the report and workspace carry today, what the tools can return, and what OrcaSlicer knows after a load that neither exposes, with the cost of each. I then kept a fact only if it answers one of the questions a first message has to settle, and only if it is cheap enough to compute at load time.

| Question the first message must settle | Fact | Today | Cost | Round 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Did the file open, and did it change my setup? | loadFacts | sent | — | unchanged |
| Can it print on the selected printer? | `placedOnBed` (OrcaSlicer's instance print-volume state) and `fitsSelectedBed` (size vs usable bed) | no; only OrcaSlicer's notice text, which means either | in memory / cheap | added |
| If not, which of my printers can? | `bedMm` per set-up printer (usable, after excluded areas); `fitsSetupPrinters` | names only | cheap | added |
| Is the model sound? | `mesh`: triangles, shells, open edges, repaired errors | only through `object_analyze` | computed at load | added |
| Is the scale right? | `unitsSuspicion` (inches or metres) | only through `object_analyze` | cheap | added when not "none" (no case exercised it) |
| How should it sit on the bed? | `asPlaced` overhang and bed contact; `betterOrientation` when much better | only through `object_analyze` | mesh pass; several minutes on the 1.26M-triangle Yoda | added, to measure its value |
| What did the file expect? | `file`: app that saved it, printer and nozzle it was made for, filament slots, painted colours | lost on a geometry-only load; otherwise only as preset names | cheap, but must be captured inside OrcaSlicer's `load_files` | added |
| Was it already prepared? | painted supports or seams, modifiers, layer ranges | partly | in memory | not exercised by these files |
| (noise) | duplicate notices; OrcaSlicer's object-info notice; `overrideCount` | sent | — | duplicates and object-info removed; `overrideCount` left in |

Left out on purpose:
- faces and holes (a heavy mesh pass);
- anything that needs a slice (support volume, time, weight);
- marketplace IDs and other metadata;
- connected-printer detail beyond its model (no case exercised it).

## Results

| Case | v0 (today) | v1 (skill) | v2 (skill + facts) |
|---|---|---|---|
| battery | 198 words: guessed purpose, orientation/support/material bullets, "check your plate" | 78 words, ready, one question | 116 words, ready ("no errors, very little prints over empty space") |
| octopus | 209 words of guesses and bullets | 101 words | 110 words |
| tiny | 202 words; calls standing on edge "the best way" | 113 words; first-layer caution | 107 words: **"lay one wall flat, contact 64 → 660 mm², no overhang"**, which only the orientation fact made possible |
| yoda | 246 words, layer and support advice | 107 words, supports | 138 words, supports, "no holes or errors" |
| frame_parts | 290 words, suggests finer presets | 138 words | 132 words |
| headband | 232 words; right printers from the model's own knowledge, Kobra 3 bed wrong | 115 words; picks the Qidi, gives the Kobra 3 as 250 mm (it is 251 usable) | 131 words; A1 or Qidi from `fitsSetupPrinters`; "switch rather than resize" |
| two_color | 363 words; **"too wide", wrong** | 181 words; **"doesn't fit the plate", wrong** | 142 words; **"hangs over the edge, has to be moved, doesn't need resizing"**, correct |
| bambu_project | 274 words | 135 words | 143 words; "every piece fits each of your printers" |

What this shows:

1. **The skill rewrite fixes the tone and length on every kind of file, not only the headband.** Median length goes from about 240 words to about 115. Today's skill requires an object guess, an orientation/supports/strength discussion and a warning-origin explanation, so even Opus writes all three for a battery holder that needs nothing.
2. **The facts fix correctness, and two of the three corrections were cases I had not looked for.**
   - **two_color:** OrcaSlicer's "laid over the boundary of plate" text covers both "too big" and "placed off the edge". Without `placedOnBed` and `fitsSelectedBed`, both v0 and v1 told the person a 244 × 129 mm object was too big for a 250 × 250 mm bed. With them, v2 said to move it.
   - **tiny:** the orientation fact turned a vague first-layer caution into a concrete fix.
   - **headband:** the bed sizes replaced guessed numbers.
3. **No fact made the replies worse.** The mesh facts mostly produce a short "no holes or errors" clause. The model ignored 193 shells on Yoda and 57 on the octopus, which is right.
4. **`overrideCount: 1` is noise.** Every freshly loaded STL carries it. Four runs stopped to wonder what it is, though none put it in the reply. Its cause is unverified.

Bold: Opus used 0–9 bold phrases per reply under every variant. That's no evidence either way about gpt-5.4-mini's heavy bolding, so nothing was changed for it.

## App defects found along the way (not fixed)

- **Blank picture.** The two_color render the app attached is completely empty: the object is partly off the plate, and the render shows nothing at all. The agent gets no picture exactly when it needs one.
- **Turn with no report.** Opening `Cura_Plus4-Pla.3mf` loaded no objects and saved no report, yet the app still started an agent turn whose only input was the workspace block. That case was dropped from the set.
- **Slow orientation scoring.** `object_analyze` with orientations on Yoda kept the app busy for several minutes. So `asPlaced` and `betterOrientation` can't be computed on every load as is. They need a cheaper current-orientation-only measure, a triangle cap, or to run after the first message.

## Proposed next steps (not started)

1. Add the facts in the table to the report: fit split into placed vs fits, beds of set-up printers, mesh health, units, file facts captured inside `load_files`, prepared-ness flags. Remove the duplicate and object-info notices, and decide what `overrideCount` should mean.
2. Decide orientation separately, once its cost on large meshes is measured properly.
3. Keep iterating the skill with this harness. The case set and recorder can be re-run in about 10 minutes, so every skill edit can be measured across all eight files.
4. Then one live gpt-5.4-mini batch on the same eight recorded requests, v0 vs the final variant (needs Kenneth's approval).

## Round 1 (headband only), for the record

This round used three runs each on a hand-rebuilt headband request:
- today's request;
- data only (bed sizes and a fit list);
- data plus the rewritten skill.

Data alone made the printer advice right but left the reply long. Only the skill rewrite fixed the tone. Round 2 confirms both findings across the eight files.

## Skill text tested (v2)

The rewrite replaced the paragraphs "Look at the attached picture… make an educated guess at what the object is, what it is likely for, and how it should be sliced…" and "Write one useful message… Explain where a warning came from…" with:

> Look at the attached picture when there is one. Check the selected printer, filament and process presets and the plate type against the file and against the printers the person has set up; when one looks wrong for this print, say which and suggest the one to use, without changing it. When an object does not fit the selected printer, name a set-up printer it fits, from fitsSetupPrinters.
>
> Write a short message, a few sentences, about what matters for this file now:
> - Lead with what decides whether or how it can print: a load that failed, an object that does not fit, a printer to choose, settings or G-code that need review. Say it once, with only the numbers that matter.
> - Say what you take the object to be, and how it should be printed, only when that changes the advice, and then briefly, as a guess. Leave other advice (material, strength, orientation) until the main decision is made.
> - Do not explain routine loading: how the file was opened, whether its settings were applied, or which notices appeared, unless it changes the next step. Do not imply that loading the file ran G-code on a printer. Never claim a warning was fixed merely because its dialog was dismissed.
> - When nothing needs attention, say so in a sentence.
> - End with one question or offer about the next step, not a menu of alternatives. Do not offer to print while the intended printer or another consequential choice is unresolved.

v2 also adds, after the setupPrinters sentence, a description of each new field. The core of it: "an object that is off the bed but fits it needs moving, not resizing". The notice table is unchanged.

The experiment files (recorder, case recorder, probe, renderer, variants, every request and reply) are in this session's scratchpad under `exp/`.

I agree, and that's how I redid it. I started from what the app knows when a file loads, kept the facts that help the first message decide something, and tested on eight different files instead of the headband alone. The rewritten skill fixed the tone and length on every file. The chosen facts corrected two replies that were wrong or vague, and neither of those was a problem I had gone looking for. The skill is not finalized and nothing in the repo has changed. - Did the file change my setup?
- Can it print on the selected printer, and if not, on which of my printers?
- Is the model sound, and is it the right scale?
- How should it sit on the bed?
- What did the file expect: which printer, which filaments, any painted colours?

Facts that need a slice or a heavy mesh pass stayed behind tools.

**How it was tested.** Each file was opened in a test copy of the app whose agent pointed at a local recorder. That gave the exact request gpt-5.4-mini would get, including the app's own picture, and nothing went to OpenAI. The extra facts came from the app's own tools, the printer profiles and the 3MF files. Each request went to a fresh Opus 5.5 subagent, one run per file and version, in three versions: today's request (v0), the rewritten skill (v1), and the rewritten skill plus the facts (v2).

**Results:**
- **Today's skill makes even Opus long-winded.** v0 replies run 198–363 words. A battery holder that needs nothing still gets a guess at what it is, bullets on orientation, supports and material, and "check your plate".
- **The skill rewrite fixes tone and length everywhere.** v1 replies run 78–181 words and lead with what matters.
- **The facts fixed things I hadn't anticipated:**
  - **Two-colour boxes:** OrcaSlicer's "laid over the boundary of plate" message means either "too big" or "placed off the edge". v0 and v1 both told the person a 244 × 129 mm object was too big for a 250 × 250 mm bed. With the facts "not placed on the bed" and "fits the bed", v2 correctly said to move it.
  - **22 mm corner piece:** it stands on thin edges with 64 mm² touching the bed. With the orientation fact, v2 suggested laying a wall flat, which gives 660 mm² of contact and no overhang. Without it, the replies only said to watch the first layer.
  - **Headband:** real bed sizes replaced the model's guesses. Without them, v1 gave the Kobra 3 as 250 mm; its usable width is 251.
- **No fact made a reply worse.** The mesh-health facts mostly add a short "no holes or errors".
- **One field is noise.** `overrideCount: 1` appears on every freshly loaded STL, and four runs stopped to wonder what it meant. Its cause is unverified.

**Limits:** one run per cell, Opus instead of gpt-5.4-mini, and I judged the replies myself.

**App defects found along the way (not fixed):**
- **Blank picture:** the picture the app attaches is completely empty when the object is partly off the plate, which is exactly when it is needed.
- **Turn with no report:** opening a Cura 3MF loaded nothing and saved no report, yet the app still started an agent turn with only the workspace block.
- **Slow orientation check:** the orientation check kept the app busy for several minutes on the 1.26-million-triangle Yoda model. It can't run on every load as it is now.

**Decisions for you:**
1. Should I build the chosen facts into the report? That means placed vs fits, the bed of each printer you've set up, mesh health, units, and the file's own facts captured during the load, plus removing the noisy notices. Orientation would wait until its cost is solved.
2. Should I keep refining the skill with this test setup? It re-runs all eight files in a few minutes. It lives in my temporary scratch folder, so I'd move it into the repo if you want to keep it.
3. Once the skill settles, may I run one live gpt-5.4-mini batch on these eight recorded requests, today's version against the final one?
